title: Weighted Reshetikhin–Turaev sewing, framing anomaly and state dimensions

items.title: Weighted modular TQFT model and physical interpretation boundary
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement:
Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular ribbon fusion category with finite simple-label set $I$, unit label $0$, simple pivotal dimensions $d_i$, twists $\theta_i$, and Hopf-link matrix $s$. Choose a square root $D\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ of $\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$ and set $S=s/D$, $p_+=\sum_{i\in I}\theta_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Modularity means that $s$ is invertible; no positivity of $d_i$ or $D$ is assumed.

Use the weighted Lagrangian ribbon-bordism category whose objects are closed oriented marked surfaces with a Lagrangian in real first homology and whose morphisms are compact oriented three-bordisms with colored ribbon graphs and integer weights. Composition adds the Walker Maslov index computed from the two individual bordism relations and the specified middle Lagrangian. For a genus-$g$ surface with ordered labels $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, write $H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*$ and

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1,W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}).$$

The weighted RT model is this category, these finite-dimensional complex state spaces, and the exact surgery-defined symmetric monoidal functor $Z$ of the supplied theorem. It includes actual coupon morphisms, disconnected bordisms and empty ends; increasing an integer weight by one multiplies the map by $\kappa$. The model retains the full anomaly and asserts no ordinary anomaly-free functor unless cancellation data are supplied separately.

items.title: Modular dimensions follow from exact sewing
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement:
Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex modular ribbon fusion category with simple-label set $I$, unit label $0$, simple dimensions $d_i$, Hopf-link matrix $s$, and a chosen square root $D$ of $\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. Put $S=s/D$ and $H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*$. In the weighted RT model, define the closed unmarked genus-$g$ state space by $V(\Sigma_g)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1,H^{\otimes g})$. For every integer $g\ge0$,

$$\dim_{\mathbb C}V(\Sigma_g)=\sum_{i\in I}S_{0i}^{\,2-2g},$$

with no complex conjugation in this formula. The sphere state space has dimension one, and the unmarked torus has dimension $|I|$ with basis $b_i:\mathbf1\to i\otimes i^*\subset H$. For every compatible separating or nonseparating circle cut, the actual normalized RT tube map from the complete direct sum of dual-label channels to the glued state space is an isomorphism; its inverse is the complete cutting resolution, retaining all multiplicities, markings, tensor orders, and Lagrangian identifications.

items.title: A nontrivial weight anomaly obstructs forgetting the weights
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement: Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences, and fix a weighted RT bordism $M$ with all its boundary data, ribbon graph, object Lagrangians, and coupons held fixed. If its integer weight is $n$, then $Z(M,n+1)=\kappa Z(M,n)$. If $\kappa\ne1$ and $Z(M,n)$ is a nonzero linear map, the weighted RT assignment cannot factor through the operation that forgets integer weights while keeping the same maps. This obstruction concerns ordinary forgetting of the weight; an anomaly-canceling enlargement or a different normalization requires separate data and is not asserted here.

title: Weighted Reshetikhin–Turaev sewing, framing anomaly and state dimensions — Examples

items.title: $SU(2)$ level $k$ has $k+1$ torus states
items.physical_scope: Pure mathematics; no physical premises or physical claim.
items.statement:
For an integer level $k\ge1$, let $\ell=k+2$ and take the actual positive-trace ribbon semisimplification of the finite-dimensional integrable type-1 Lusztig divided-power $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ tilting modules at $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$. Its simple labels are $a=0,1,\ldots,k$, and its normalized matrix is

$$S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{k+2}}\sin\!\left(\frac{(a+1)(b+1)\pi}{k+2}\right),\qquad 0\le a,b\le k.$$

Its unmarked torus state space has dimension $k+1$. At $k=1$, its closed genus-$g$ state-space dimension is $2^g$ for every integer $g\ge0$. These are mathematical consequences for the specified tilting quotient, not claims about a physical realization.

references.title: Stephen F. Sawin, Quantum Groups at Roots of Unity and Modularity, arXiv:math/0308281v2
